articles.title: The Gita Begins With a Breakdown, Not a Sermon
articles.titleHinglish: Gita Bhaashan Se Nahi, Ek Toot Jaane Se Shuru Hoti Hai
articles.content:
People treat the Gita as a book of instructions delivered from above. It is worth remembering how it starts. A capable man, at the most important moment of his life, sits down in his chariot and says he cannot do it. His hands are shaking. His mouth is dry. He says his mind is whirling and he cannot see what is right.

That is a panic attack, described accurately several thousand years ago.

What matters is what happens next, because it is not what most advice does. Krishna does not say cheer up. He does not say you are overreacting, or think positive. The conversation that follows is long, and it takes Arjuna's collapse seriously enough to answer it properly rather than quickly.

This alone is worth taking from it. When someone in front of you is falling apart, the useful response is rarely a slogan. It is a real conversation that treats their confusion as legitimate.

The second thing worth noticing is what Arjuna's crisis actually is. It is not lack of skill or courage. He is caught between duties that genuinely conflict — his role as a warrior, his love for the family standing opposite him, his sense of what is right. That is what makes it recognisable. Most modern paralysis is the same shape: a job that pays and a job that means something, a parent's expectation and your own life, staying for someone and leaving for yourself. The problem is not that you do not know what is right. The problem is that two things you believe in point in different directions.

And the third: Krishna's answer is not to remove the difficulty. Arjuna does not get an easy way out, and he is not told the situation is less painful than it looks. He is given a way to act inside it — with clarity about what is his to control, without ownership of the result, and without pretending the pain is not there.

That is why the book has lasted. It is not comfort literature. It is a manual for functioning when a situation is genuinely bad and someone still has to act.

So if you have only ever encountered the Gita as a set of quotes on social media, it is worth going back to the first chapter, where a strong man says plainly that he cannot go on. Almost everyone has had that day. Very few sacred books begin there, and it is exactly why this one is still being read.
articles.contentHinglish:
Log Gita ko upar se diye gaye hidayat-naame ki tarah lete hain. Yeh yaad rakhne laayak hai ki wo shuru kaise hoti hai. Ek kaabil aadmi, apni zindagi ke sabse zaroori lamhe par, apne rath mein baith jaata hai aur kehta hai ki usse nahi hoga. Uske haath kaanp rahe hain. Muh sookh raha hai. Wo kehta hai uska mann ghoom raha hai aur use dikh hi nahi raha ki sahi kya hai.

Yeh panic attack hai, hazaaron saal pehle theek theek likha hua.

Mayne yeh rakhta hai ki aage kya hota hai, kyunki zyadatar salaah aisa nahi karti. Krishna yeh nahi kehte ki khush ho jao. Wo yeh nahi kehte ki tum overreact kar rahe ho, ya positive socho. Uske baad ki baat-cheet lambi hai, aur wo Arjun ke toot jaane ko itni gambhirta se leti hai ki jawab jaldi mein nahi, theek se deti hai.

Sirf yahi baat lene laayak hai. Jab saamne koi bikhar raha ho, kaam ka jawab shayad hi koi slogan hota hai. Kaam ki cheez ek asli baat-cheet hai jo unki uljhan ko jayaz maanti hai.

Doosri gaur karne laayak baat yeh hai ki Arjun ka sankat asal mein hai kya. Wo kaabiliyat ya himmat ki kami nahi hai. Wo do aise kartavyon ke beech phansa hai jo sach mein takra rahe hain — yoddha ka kirdaar, saamne khade parivaar se pyaar, aur uski apni sahi-galat ki samajh. Isiliye wo pehchaana hua lagta hai. Aaj ka zyadatar jam jaana isi shakal ka hai: wo job jo paisa deti hai aur wo jo matlab deti hai, maa-baap ki ummeed aur apni zindagi, kisi ke liye rukna aur khud ke liye jaana. Dikkat yeh nahi hai ki aapko pata nahi ki sahi kya hai. Dikkat yeh hai ki jin do cheezon par aap yakeen karte ho wo alag disha dikha rahi hain.

Aur teesri: Krishna ka jawab mushkil ko hata dena nahi hai. Arjun ko aasaan raasta nahi milta, aur use yeh bhi nahi bataya jaata ki sthiti dikhne se kam dukhad hai. Use us sthiti ke andar rehte hue kaam karne ka tareeka milta hai — is saaf samajh ke saath ki uske haath mein kya hai, phal ka maalik bane bina, aur dard ke na hone ka dikhawa kiye bina.

Isiliye yeh kitab tiki hui hai. Yeh tasalli ka saahitya nahi hai. Yeh us waqt kaam karne ki guide hai jab haalat sach mein kharab ho aur phir bhi kisi ko kadam uthana ho.

Toh agar aapne Gita ko sirf social media ke quotes ki tarah dekha hai, to pehle adhyay par lautna zaroori hai — jahan ek majboot aadmi saaf saaf kehta hai ki ab usse aage nahi bada jaata. Lagbhag har kisi ka aisa ek din raha hai. Bahut kam pavitra granth wahan se shuru hote hain, aur theek isiliye yeh aaj bhi padha ja raha hai.

articles.title: Work Fully, Own the Result Lightly
articles.titleHinglish: Poori Mehnat Karo, Nateeje Ko Halka Pakdo
articles.content:
Karmanye vadhikaraste ma phaleshu kadachana is probably the most quoted line in Indian life and one of the most misunderstood. It is regularly used to mean do not expect anything, or worse, do not care. Both readings would have surprised the man saying it, since the entire conversation is aimed at getting someone to act.

The more accurate reading is a description of ownership. You own the action. The result is produced by your action plus a hundred other factors — timing, other people, the market, health, luck. Claiming ownership of something with a hundred authors is what creates suffering, because you take full responsibility for an outcome you only partly controlled.

This is not a licence for indifference. In fact it demands more effort, not less, because once the result is out of your hands the only place your attention can go is the quality of the work.

What does this look like on an ordinary week?

You prepare thoroughly for the interview. You do not spend the three days afterwards replaying it, because that portion is finished and no amount of review changes it.

You raise your child with attention and honesty. You accept that they will become a person of their own making, and that a good outcome was never something you could guarantee by effort alone.

You tell someone the truth, kindly. You do not get to control whether they hear it well.

There is a psychological benefit that is easy to verify. Anxiety lives mostly in the gap between effort and outcome — the waiting, the checking, the imagining. Placing your identity in the work rather than the result shrinks that gap considerably. You still want the result. You are simply no longer using it to decide whether you were worth anything.

And there is a practical benefit too. People who are attached to results tend to make worse decisions, because fear of a bad outcome makes them cautious in exactly the places where courage was required. Detachment, honestly practised, makes you steadier, not lazier.

One caution about misuse, since this line is often used to dismiss legitimate ambition or to tell someone to stop asking for what they are owed. Not expecting the fruit does not mean not asking for your salary, not seeking justice, or not wanting a better life. It means not staking your peace on an outcome that was always going to be decided by more than you.
articles.contentHinglish:
"Karmanye vadhikaraste ma phaleshu kadachana" shayad Indian zindagi ki sabse zyada quote ki gayi line hai aur sabse zyada galat samjhi gayi bhi. Iska matlab aksar yeh nikaal liya jaata hai ki kuch ummeed mat rakho, ya usse bhi bura, parwaah mat karo. Dono padhai us aadmi ko chaunka deti jo yeh bol raha tha, kyunki poori baat-cheet ka maqsad hi kisi ko kaam par lagana tha.

Zyada sahi padhai maalikana haq ka varnan hai. Karm par aapka haq hai. Nateeja aapke karm plus sau doosri cheezon se banta hai — timing, doosre log, market, sehat, kismat. Jis cheez ke sau lekhak hon uspar maalikana haq jataana hi dukh banata hai, kyunki aap us nateeje ki poori zimmedari le lete ho jispar aapka zor aadha bhi nahi tha.

Yeh udaseenta ka license nahi hai. Balki yeh zyada mehnat maangta hai, kam nahi — kyunki jab nateeja haath se bahar hai to aapka dhyan sirf kaam ki quality par hi ja sakta hai.

Ek aam hafte mein yeh dikhta kaisa hai?

Aap interview ki poori taiyari karte ho. Uske baad ke teen din use dobara chala kar nahi bitaate, kyunki wo hissa poora ho chuka hai aur kitni bhi review usse badal nahi sakti.

Aap apne bachche ko dhyan aur imaandaari se paalte ho. Aap yeh sweekar karte ho ki wo apni banawat ka insaan banega, aur achha nateeja aisa kabhi tha hi nahi jise sirf mehnat se guarantee kiya ja sake.

Aap kisi ko sach bolte ho, narmi se. Wo use achhe se lega ya nahi — yeh aapke haath mein nahi.

Ek manovaigyanik faayda hai jise jaancha ja sakta hai. Anxiety zyadatar mehnat aur nateeje ke beech ke gap mein rehti hai — intezaar, baar baar check karna, kalpana. Apni pehchaan ko nateeje ki jagah kaam mein rakhna us gap ko kaafi chhota kar deta hai. Aap nateeja ab bhi chahte ho. Bas ab aap usse yeh tay nahi kar rahe ki aapki keemat kuch thi bhi ya nahi.

Aur ek practical faayda bhi hai. Jo log nateeje se chipke hote hain wo aksar bure faisle lete hain, kyunki bure nateeje ka dar unhe theek wahan saavdhan bana deta hai jahan himmat chahiye thi. Imaandaari se ki gayi anasakti aapko sthir banati hai, aalsi nahi.

Galat istemaal par ek chetavani, kyunki is line ka istemaal aksar jayaz mahatvakanksha ko dabaane ya kisi ko uska haq maangne se rokne ke liye hota hai. Phal ki ichha na rakhna ka matlab yeh nahi ki apni salary mat maango, insaaf mat maango, ya behtar zindagi mat chaaho. Iska matlab hai apna chain us nateeje par mat lagao jo hamesha se aapse zyada cheezon par tay hone wala tha.

articles.title: Sthitpragya: Steadiness in an Ordinary Week
articles.titleHinglish: Sthitpragya: Ek Aam Hafte Mein Sthirta
articles.content:
The Gita describes a person of steady wisdom — sthitpragya — as someone who is not thrown by pleasure or pain, praise or blame. It sounds like a description of a statue, and it is usually read as an impossible standard for saints.

It is more useful read as a description of a skill you can practise in small amounts.

Start with what it is not. It is not the absence of feeling. It is not politeness, or a flat expression, or the person who says everything is fine while their jaw is tight. Suppression produces the appearance of steadiness and none of the substance, and it costs more than the storm it hides.

What is being described is closer to this: the ability to feel something fully without being commanded by it.

An ordinary week gives you many chances to practise. Someone praises you in a meeting; notice the lift, enjoy it, and do not spend the afternoon rearranging your self-image around it. Someone criticises you; notice the sting, look at whether it is accurate, and take the accurate part. Both responses are the same skill — receiving something without letting it decide who you are.

The practical measure is not whether you felt calm. It is how long it took to come back. Everyone gets pulled off centre; the question is whether the return takes four days or four minutes. That is a trainable number, and it shortens with practice in a way that is genuinely noticeable within a few months.

A few things that help.

Do not make decisions at the peak of either state. Success makes people overcommit and failure makes them quit. The Gita's steadiness is largely about not letting the extremes of a Tuesday write the plan for the year.

Watch the mood after praise as carefully as the mood after blame. Most people only practise on the bad days, but attachment to praise is what makes blame unbearable in the first place. They are the same hook, held from two ends.

And give yourself the same treatment on both sides. If you would not let one criticism define you, do not let one compliment do it either.

One honest note. Nobody is steady all the time, and the text is not asking for a permanent state on Tuesday of week one. It is describing a direction. A person who has practised for years still gets angry, still grieves, still feels the sting of being overlooked. What changes is the recovery, and over a life, the recovery is most of what separates a peaceful person from an exhausted one.
articles.contentHinglish:
Gita sthitpragya — sthir buddhi wale insaan — ko aisa batati hai jo sukh-dukh, taarif-nindа se hilta nahi. Sunne mein kisi murti ka varnan lagta hai, aur ise aksar sant logon ke liye namumkin paimana samajh liya jaata hai.

Ise ek hunar ki tarah padhna zyada kaam ka hai — jise thodi thodi maatra mein practise kiya ja sakta hai.

Pehle yeh ki wo hai kya nahi. Wo feelings ka na hona nahi hai. Wo shishtachaar nahi hai, na flat chehra, na wo insaan jo jabda kasa hue "sab theek hai" bolta hai. Dabaana sthirta ka dikhava banata hai aur asliyat kuch nahi, aur uski keemat us toofan se zyada hoti hai jise wo chhupa raha hai.

Jo batayaa ja raha hai wo isse kareeb hai: kisi cheez ko poora mehsoos karna aur phir bhi uske hukum mein na aana.

Ek aam hafta practise ke bahut mauke deta hai. Meeting mein koi taarif karta hai; us uthaan ko dekho, mazaa lo, aur poori dopahar apni image ko uske aas paas mat sajao. Koi criticism karta hai; chubhan dekho, jaancho ki wo sahi hai ya nahi, aur sahi hissa le lo. Dono jawab ek hi hunar hain — kuch lena, bina use yeh tay karne diye ki aap kaun ho.

Practical paimana yeh nahi hai ki aapko shaanti mehsoos hui ya nahi. Paimana yeh hai ki wapas aane mein kitna waqt laga. Sabhi kendra se hilte hain; sawaal yeh hai ki wapsi mein chaar din lagte hain ya chaar minute. Yeh number sudhaara ja sakta hai, aur kuch mahino mein iska chhota hona sach mein mehsoos hota hai.

Kuch cheezein jo madad karti hain.

Dono halaton ke peak par faisla mat lo. Safalta logon se zyada commitments karwa deti hai aur asafalta unse chhudwa deti hai. Gita wali sthirta zyadatar isi baare mein hai ki ek Mangalvaar ke charam saal ka plan na likh dein.

Taarif ke baad ka mood utni hi gaur se dekho jitna nindа ke baad ka. Zyadatar log sirf bure dinon par practise karte hain, par taarif se judav hi nindа ko asahniya banata hai. Wo ek hi kaanta hai, do sire se pakda hua.

Aur dono taraf khud ke saath ek jaisa bartav karo. Agar ek criticism ko apni pehchaan nahi banne doge, to ek taarif ko bhi mat banne do.

Ek imaandaar baat. Koi hamesha sthir nahi hota, aur granth pehle hafte ke Mangalvaar ko permanent halat nahi maang raha. Wo ek disha bata raha hai. Jo saalon se practise kar raha hai use bhi gussa aata hai, gham hota hai, nazarandaaz kiye jaane ki chubhan hoti hai. Jo badalta hai wo wapsi ka waqt hai — aur ek zindagi mein, wahi wapsi shaant insaan aur thake hue insaan ke beech ka zyadatar farq hai.
